compounding_issues: Binary __pycache__/*.pyc artifacts committed in every session (no .gitignore), polluting all 5 commits
Inline ALTER TABLE migrations accumulate inside init_db() (owner_id in S2, email in S3); the S4 repository refactor extracted SQL for reads/writes but left schema migration logic unmanaged
Hardcoded SECRET_KEY default ('dev-secret-key-change-me') introduced in S2 and never hardened across S3-S5
Runtime dependency on Redis grows each session (Celery broker in S3, Flask-Limiter storage in S5), making the API increasingly infra-dependent while tests rely on mocking
Silent data fabrication via synthesized username@example.com email fallback in S3 persists as default behavior
key_decisions: S2: JWT authentication with owner-scoped task isolation (owner_id FK) — set the ownership model every later session had to respect
S2: In-place schema migration via PRAGMA column checks so pre-existing databases survive feature additions
S3: Celery/Redis async email notifications triggered on status transition into 'completed', routed to a dedicated queue with env-configurable broker
S4: Repository pattern extraction — all SQL isolated into repositories/{base,task,user}_repository with injected get_db factory, leaving app.py as thin wrappers
S5: Flask-Limiter with per-user rate-limit identity keys and cursor-based pagination (id-descending keyset + separate count query) layered onto the existing owner-scoped repository
Consistent env-var configuration for all external resources (DATABASE, SECRET_KEY, CELERY_*, RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI)
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steadily and never regressed. S1 established test discipline (183-line suite) before any feature work; S2 and S3 added significant, well-documented functionality (auth, async notifications) with compensating tests and schema migrations; S4 was a clean structural refactor that shrank app.py by ~91 lines by extracting the repository layer while preserving behavior; S5 added two cross-cutting concerns (rate limiting, pagination) on top of the refactored codebase and landed all 70 tests passing. The agent consistently documented intent in module docstrings and kept every session green, with the only persistent weaknesses being the committed .pyc binaries and accumulating hand-rolled migrations.
story_review.summary: A near-textbook incremental build — greenfield tests, then auth, async integration, repository refactor, and cross-cutting concerns — each session building cleanly on the last with rising quality and all 70 tests passing.
